# Sirach 43 — Disagreement Log

**Chapter:** Sirach 43 | **Date:** 2026-03-17 | **Total Disagreements:** 22

---

## Disagreement 1 — 43:1, "pride" vs. "crown" vs. "vault"

**EMET:** "The pride of the heavenly heights is the clear firmament"
**LOGOS:** "The pride of the heights above is the clear vault of heaven"
**PNEUMA:** "The vault of heaven, crystalline and clear, is the crown of the heights"
**Issue:** Greek kauchēma = boast, glory, pride. EMET/LOGOS retain "pride"; PNEUMA restructures entirely. "Firmament" vs. "vault" for stereōma.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "crown of the heights" + "clear firmament" — combining PNEUMA's elevation with EMET's biblical "firmament" (echo of Genesis 1).

---

## Disagreement 2 — 43:2, "proclaims" vs. "makes proclamation" vs. "announces itself"

**EMET:** "proclaims as it rises"
**LOGOS:** "makes proclamation as it rises"
**PNEUMA:** "announces itself"
**Issue:** Greek anaggellōn = proclaiming, announcing. EMET/LOGOS are close; PNEUMA's reflexive rendering loses the sense that the sun proclaims God's glory.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts EMET: "proclaims as it rises."

---

## Disagreement 3 — 43:2, "marvelous instrument" vs. "marvelous creation"

**EMET:** "a marvelous instrument, the work of the Most High"
**LOGOS:** "a marvelous creation, the work of the Most High"
**PNEUMA:** "what a marvel it is! What a work of the Most High!"
**Issue:** Greek thaumasion poiēma = marvelous work/creation. "Instrument" (EMET) implies tool; "creation" (LOGOS) implies made thing. PNEUMA uses exclamation marks.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "marvelous creation" (LOGOS) — the sun is made, not merely instrumental.

---

## Disagreement 4 — 43:4, "blinds the eyes" vs. "dazzles the eyes"

**EMET:** "it blinds the eyes"
**LOGOS:** "it dazzles the eyes"
**PNEUMA:** "dazzles the eyes with its light"
**Issue:** Greek katablaptei tous ophthalmous = damages/impairs the eyes. EMET "blinds" is strong (perhaps too strong for ordinary sunlight); LOGOS "dazzles" is gentler.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "dazzles" as more accurate to the Greek.

---

## Disagreement 5 — 43:5, "speeds on its way" vs. "runs swiftly on its course"

**EMET:** "it speeds on its way"
**LOGOS:** "it runs swiftly on its course"
**PNEUMA:** "it races on its course"
**Issue:** Greek trechei = it runs. LOGOS is most literal; PNEUMA's "races" is vivid; EMET "speeds" is idiomatic.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "runs swiftly on its course" (LOGOS) — closest to Greek.

---

## Disagreement 6 — 43:6, "provides a marker of times" vs. "marks the passage of time"

**EMET:** "provides a marker of times and a sign of the world"
**LOGOS:** "it is a sign of seasons and an everlasting symbol"
**PNEUMA:** "a sign of seasons and a signal for the world"
**Issue:** Greek sēmeion aiōnos = sign of the age/eternity. LOGOS adds "everlasting symbol" for aiōnos. EMET "sign of the world" is more literal.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "a sign of seasons and an everlasting marker" — capturing both temporal and eternal dimensions.

---

## Disagreement 7 — 43:7, "feast days" vs. "feast days"

**EMET:** "the sign of feast days"
**LOGOS:** "the reckoning of feast days"
**PNEUMA:** "the reckoning of feast days"
**Issue:** Greek sēmeion heortēs = sign/reckoning of feast. LOGOS/PNEUMA agree; EMET "sign" is more literal but LOGOS "reckoning" better captures the calendrical function.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "the reckoning of feast days."

---

## Disagreement 8 — 43:8, "military instrument" vs. "instrument of the host on high"

**EMET:** "a military instrument in the heights above"
**LOGOS:** "an instrument of the host on high"
**PNEUMA:** "guiding the armies of heaven on high"
**Issue:** Greek skeuos stratopedōn = equipment of military camps, or instrument of armies. The moon signals the calendar for military expeditions. LOGOS "host on high" has a celestial/angelic double meaning.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "instrument of the host on high" — preserving the celestial-military ambiguity.

---

## Disagreement 9 — 43:9, "beauty of heaven" vs. "brilliance of the stars" vs. "splendor of the stars"

**EMET:** "The beauty of heaven, the glory of the stars"
**LOGOS:** "The brilliance of the stars is the glory of the skies"
**PNEUMA:** "The splendor of the stars — glory of the skies!"
**Issue:** Greek kosmos ouranōn = adornment/glory of the heavens. "Beauty" (EMET) is literal; "brilliance" (LOGOS) adds light quality; "splendor" (PNEUMA) is elevated.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "The splendor of the stars is the glory of the skies" — most elevated for the hymn register.

---

## Disagreement 10 — 43:10, "stand in judgment" vs. "stand in due order" vs. "stand in formation"

**EMET:** "they stand in judgment"
**LOGOS:** "they stand in due order"
**PNEUMA:** "they stand in formation"
**Issue:** Greek en taxei autōn = in their order/rank. EMET "stand in judgment" may reflect variant reading; LOGOS/PNEUMA correctly render "in their order."
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "stand in due order" (LOGOS).

---

## Disagreement 11 — 43:11, "exceedingly beautiful in its splendor" vs. "surpassing loveliness" vs. "extraordinary beauty"

**EMET:** "it is exceedingly beautiful in its splendor"
**LOGOS:** "it shines with a surpassing loveliness"
**PNEUMA:** "it blazes with extraordinary beauty"
**Issue:** Greek hōraiotēti autou sphodra = very beautiful in its beauty/seasonableness. "Loveliness" (LOGOS) is apt but perhaps too delicate; "extraordinary beauty" (PNEUMA) is clear.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "it blazes with extraordinary beauty" — the verb captures both light and quality.

---

## Disagreement 12 — 43:12, "glorious arc" vs. "radiant bow" vs. "radiant arc"

**EMET:** "with its glorious arc"
**LOGOS:** "with a radiant bow"
**PNEUMA:** "in its radiant arc"
**Issue:** Greek en kraugazon tōi tokō — "the rainbow curves with its bow-shape." "Arc" vs. "bow" — both are legitimate.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "its radiant bow" — "bow" retains the Hebrew qeshet/toxon connection.

---

## Disagreement 13 — 43:13, "lightnings of his judgment" vs. "flashes of his judgment"

**EMET:** "lightnings of his judgment"
**LOGOS:** "flashes of his judgment"
**PNEUMA:** "flashes of his judgment"
**Issue:** Greek astrapas kritikás = lightnings of judgment. EMET "lightnings" is more literal; LOGOS/PNEUMA "flashes" is more natural English.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "flashes of his judgment" — "flashes" is accurate and avoids the plural awkwardness of "lightnings."

---

## Disagreement 14 — 43:15, "makes the clouds firm" vs. "densifies the clouds" vs. "makes the clouds dense"

**EMET:** "In his might he makes the clouds firm"
**LOGOS:** "In his majesty he densifies the clouds"
**PNEUMA:** "In his might he makes the clouds dense"
**Issue:** Greek en ischui autou epistasen nephelas = in his strength he solidified the clouds. LOGOS "densifies" is technically accurate but awkward. "Majesty" vs. "might" for ischus.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "In his majesty he makes the clouds dense."

---

## Disagreement 15 — 43:16, earth "writhe" vs. "quake"

**EMET:** "makes the earth writhe"
**LOGOS:** "makes the earth quake"
**PNEUMA:** "shakes the earth"
**Issue:** Greek ōdinēsei = to be in labor pains, to writhe. "Writhe" (EMET) is most literal and powerful; "quake" (LOGOS) is conventional.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA retains "writhe" — the birth-labor imagery is intentional and should be preserved.

---

## Disagreement 16 — 43:22, "sudden cloudburst" vs. "sudden mist" vs. "mist"

**EMET:** "A sudden cloudburst heals all these"
**LOGOS:** "But a sudden mist brings healing to all these"
**PNEUMA:** "Then a mist rolls in and heals everything"
**Issue:** Greek erchomenē nephalē = coming cloud. "Cloudburst" (EMET) implies rain; "mist" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) implies fog. The verse is a reversal after the burning frost — healing moisture.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "sudden mist" as more accurate — the context suggests soft relief, not violent rain.

---

## Disagreement 17 — 43:23, "planning" vs. "counsel" vs. "wisdom"

**EMET:** "By his planning he has stilled the deep"
**LOGOS:** "By his counsel he has stilled the ocean deep"
**PNEUMA:** "By his wisdom he calmed the great deep"
**Issue:** Greek boule = counsel, deliberate purpose. "Counsel" (LOGOS) is most accurate; "planning" (EMET) is functional; "wisdom" (PNEUMA) is interpretive.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "By his counsel he has stilled the deep."

---

## Disagreement 18 — 43:25, description of sea creatures

**EMET:** "strange and various creatures, all kinds of living things"
**LOGOS:** "all manner of strange and varied creatures, the whole teeming world of living things"
**PNEUMA:** "strange and wonderful creatures of every kind, all manner of living things"
**Issue:** LOGOS expands "teeming world" without clear Greek support. PNEUMA adds "wonderful." EMET is most compact.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "all manner of strange and varied creatures, the whole teeming world of living things" — "teeming" captures the Greek sense of abundance.

---

## Disagreement 19 — 43:26, "messenger succeeds" — what is the messenger?

**EMET:** "Because of him his messenger succeeds"
**LOGOS:** "Because of him his messenger succeeds"
**PNEUMA:** "Because of him his messenger accomplishes its task"
**Issue:** Greek angelos = messenger/angel. The verse is cryptic. All agents interpret "messenger" as the divine word or angel. EMET/LOGOS agree verbatim; PNEUMA expands.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS.

---

## Disagreement 20 — 43:27, THE KEY VERSE — "he is the all"

**EMET:** "he is the all"
**LOGOS:** "He is the all"
**PNEUMA:** "He is the all"
**Issue:** Greek autos estin to pan = he himself is the all/everything. This is the theological climax — all three agents independently render this the same way. No softening to "he is in all things" or "he is above all."
**Resolution:** SOPHIA retains "He is the all" — unanimous. The near-pantheistic formula must stand.

---

## Disagreement 21 — 43:30, structure of the exhortation

**EMET:** "When you praise the Lord, exalt him as much as you can; for he will surpass even that. When you exalt him, redouble your strength, do not weary, for you cannot reach the end."
**LOGOS:** "Exalt the Lord as highly as you can, for he will surpass you. When you exalt him, gather all your strength; do not grow weary, for you cannot come to the end."
**PNEUMA:** "Praise the Lord and lift him as high as you can — he still surpasses you. Summon all your strength to exalt him; do not grow tired, for you will never reach the end."
**Issue:** The verse has a building, climactic structure that all agents capture differently. The key is preserving the three movements: exalt → he surpasses → still exalt more.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA restructures: "Exalt the Lord as highly as you can, for he will surpass even that. When you exalt him, redouble your strength; do not grow weary, for you cannot reach the end."

---

## Disagreement 22 — 43:33, "godly" vs. "devout" vs. "faithful"

**EMET:** "to the godly he has granted wisdom"
**LOGOS:** "to the devout he has given wisdom"
**PNEUMA:** "to those who are faithful he has given wisdom"
**Issue:** Greek eusebousin = to the devout/pious. "Devout" (LOGOS) is most precise; "godly" (EMET) is biblical English; "faithful" (PNEUMA) shifts the meaning slightly.
**Resolution:** SOPHIA adopts "devout" as the most precise rendering of eusebousin.

---

*Total disagreements logged: 22*
